explanation: Unlike in parts of the Middle East, Africa, and South Asia where the left hand is reserved for hygiene and seen as unclean, Spain has no such taboo. Spanish table manners follow the continental European style — fork in the left hand, knife in the right, both hands visible on the table — but switching hands or using your left hand for bread or finger food causes no offense.
local_tip: Eat normally with either hand; just keep both hands visible on the table rather than in your lap, which is the real Spanish table-manners rule to know.

also_check.note: The left hand is traditionally reserved for hygiene, so eating or passing food with it is considered unclean.
As in much of the Arab world, the left hand is used for washing, so eating or offering food with it is frowned upon.
Islamic etiquette calls for eating and passing dishes with the right hand only.

sources.title: Spanish table manners: do you know the rules?
